blogPosts.title: How Often Should You Mow Your Lawn in St Kilda East?
blogPosts.excerpt: Discover the ideal mowing frequency for a healthy St Kilda East lawn, considering local grass types, bayside climate, and seasonal growth patterns for best results.
body: Determining the perfect mowing schedule for your St Kilda East lawn depends on several local factors. The bayside climate, with its relatively mild winters and warm summers, means grass growth doesn't fully stop. During the peak growing season from October to March, most cool-season grasses common in Melbourne's inner suburbs, like ryegrass and fescue, will need mowing every 7 to 10 days. This frequency encourages dense growth, which naturally chokes out weeds and creates a lush, resilient turf.

In the cooler months from April to September, growth slows considerably. You can often extend the time between mows to every 3 to 4 weeks for St Kilda East lawns. However, it's crucial not to let it get too long, as this can shade the soil and promote fungal diseases, especially with the occasional damp, overcast days typical of a Port Phillip Bay winter. A good rule of thumb is the one-third rule: never remove more than one-third of the grass blade in a single cut, as this stresses the plant.

The type of grass you have in St Kilda East will also dictate the schedule. Buffalo grass varieties like Sir Walter are popular for their shade tolerance and lower water needs, while kikuyu is a vigorous, sun-loving option. Each has a slightly different growth habit and ideal mowing height. Our team at All Good Garden Care identifies your grass type during our initial assessment and provides a tailored maintenance plan that keeps your St Kilda East lawn in peak condition throughout the year.

Beyond frequency, mowing technique matters. Cutting at the right height—generally between 3-5cm for most residential lawns—promotes root depth and drought resistance. This is particularly important for St Kilda East gardens exposed to summer sea breezes. Regular, correct mowing is the single most important task for a great-looking lawn. If you're unsure about the right schedule for your specific garden, a professional assessment can make all the difference.

blogPosts.title: Best Native Plants for St Kilda East Coastal Gardens
blogPosts.excerpt: Learn which hardy Australian natives thrive in St Kilda East's coastal conditions, offering low-maintenance beauty and support for local wildlife.
body: St Kilda East's proximity to Port Phillip Bay creates a unique microclimate for gardens, with salt-laden winds and sandy soils being common challenges. Choosing the right plants is key to a low-maintenance, thriving garden. Australian native plants are superbly adapted to these conditions. Plants like Coastal Rosemary (Westringia fruticosa) are incredibly hardy, tolerate salt spray, and can be shaped into dense, formal hedges that provide excellent privacy.

For larger feature plants, the Coastal Banksia (Banksia integrifolia) is a stunning choice, offering unique flower spikes that attract native birds. Its leathery leaves are tough against wind and salt. In shaded areas under existing trees, Correa reflexa (Common Correa) provides beautiful, bell-shaped flowers in winter, offering crucial nectar for birds when other food sources are scarce. These selections directly support the local St Kilda East ecosystem.

Groundcovers are essential for weed suppression and adding texture. Myoporum parvifolium is a fantastic, fast-growing groundcover with small white flowers that spreads to cover bare soil quickly, reducing maintenance. For a splash of colour, Chrysocephalum apiculatum (Yellow Buttons) forms a tough mat with bright yellow flowers. Using these plants in St Kilda East gardens means less watering, less fertilising, and more enjoyment.

When planting in St Kilda East, soil preparation is still important. Amending sandy soils with compost and organic matter before planting will give your natives the best start. Applying a layer of coarse mulch helps retain moisture and keep roots cool. Our team at All Good Garden Care can help you design and plant a beautiful, sustainable native garden perfectly suited to your St Kilda East property's specific conditions and your personal taste.

blogPosts.title: Preparing Your St Kilda East Garden for Melbourne Winters
blogPosts.excerpt: A step-by-step guide to protecting your St Kilda East garden from frost, wind, and wet conditions during the cooler months.
body: As autumn turns to winter in Melbourne, St Kilda East gardens need specific preparation to withstand the cooler, wetter months. The first step is a thorough autumn clean-up. Remove fallen leaves, spent annuals, and decaying debris from garden beds. This reduces hiding places for pests and fungal spores that thrive in damp conditions, giving your garden a healthy start to winter.

Pruning is essential before winter sets in. For most deciduous plants, late autumn is the ideal time for structural pruning, as the bare branches make it easy to see the plant's framework. Cut out dead, diseased, or crossing branches to improve air circulation. However, avoid pruning spring-flowering shrubs like camellias, as you'll remove next year's flowers. For hedges, a final trim before the cold will keep them tidy.

Protecting vulnerable plants from frost is crucial, even in relatively mild bayside St Kilda East. Frost cloth or even old sheets can be draped over tender plants like grevilleas or young citrus on cold nights. For potted plants, moving them closer to the house or under an eave can provide enough protection. Applying a thick layer of mulch around the base of plants insulates roots from temperature fluctuations.

Finally, winter is the perfect time for planning. Assess what worked in your garden over summer and start sketching ideas for new beds or plant additions. It's also a good time to service and clean gardening tools, ensuring they're ready for the spring burst of growth. A little work in winter ensures your St Kilda East garden will explode back into life when the warmer weather returns.

body: In the sought-after suburb of St Kilda East, first impressions matter. The front garden is the first thing visitors, potential buyers, and neighbours see. A well-maintained garden with healthy lawns, neat hedges, and tidy beds significantly boosts curb appeal and can positively influence property value. It signals that the entire property has been cared for, creating a positive perception that extends beyond the garden gate.

Beyond financial value, regular maintenance dramatically enhances your personal enjoyment of your home. A tidy, healthy outdoor space becomes an extension of your living area—a place to relax, entertain, and connect with nature. Coming home to a neat garden reduces stress and provides a sense of pride and accomplishment, even if the hard work is done by a professional team.

Consistent care also prevents small issues from becoming large, expensive problems. Regular pruning stops plants from outgrowing their space and damaging fences or structures. Weed management prevents invasive species from establishing. Early detection of pests or diseases during routine maintenance allows for simple, targeted treatments rather than drastic measures later.

Furthermore, a well-kept garden contributes positively to the entire St Kilda East neighbourhood. It fosters a sense of community pride and can encourage neighbours to maintain their own properties. By investing in regular garden maintenance with a local team like All Good, you're not just caring for your own plot; you're contributing to the overall leafy, attractive character that makes St Kilda East such a wonderful place to live.
